title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to test whether constrained prompting plus a deterministic generate→verify→repair loop (≤1 repair) increases deterministic-verifier semantic-correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level device configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic intents from a deterministic generator, execution-semantic = shared_initial_candidate (one initial sampled candidate reused across conditions per intent), model = gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Results (artifact-grounded): baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Provider accounting: completed episodes = 300; model_calls_used = 151; staged counts: shared_initial_generation = 150; repair = 1. Interpretation: under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics the guarded pipeline produced a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over a near-ceiling baseline; the run therefore invalidated the preregistered power assumption and highlights the need for baseline-calibration pilots in preregistered NetOps trials. The archived execution and analysis artifacts support all reported numbers.

sections.introduction: Natural-language intent interfaces promise to reduce operator burden by letting humans express desired network changes as free text that is automatically translated into device configuration commands. Prior work reports that single-pass LLM outputs can contain syntactic errors, omissions, or ordering violations that would violate operational invariants if applied directly. A common mitigation is a generate→verify→repair architecture in which a candidate is produced by a generator, checked by a deterministic verifier, and repaired automatically or via human review when violations occur. Our preregistered confirmatory question was narrow and operational: does constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase deterministic-verifier semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation versus an unconstrained baseline under a paired design? We preregistered the trial (study_cand_2026_b2_v1), froze the analysis plan, and executed the run under enforced adapter semantics that reuse the same initial sampled candidate across conditions (shared_initial_candidate). Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifact-backed paired trial measuring deterministic-verifier pass/fail on a synthetic corpus (N=150 paired intents). (2) Artifact-grounded outcomes showing baseline = 149/150 and guarded = 150/150 under shared_initial_candidate semantics, with paired difference ≈0.67 pp (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00,0.02]). (3) A methodological recommendation that preregistered NetOps trials include short baseline-calibration pilots and explicitly state generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate vs independent sampling) because those semantics change the estimand and interpretation.
sections.related_work: Related literature spans intent-translation evaluations, verifier-guided repair systems, deterministic formal verifiers, and analyses of agentic/tool-augmented safety. Intent-driven translation and evaluation studies report that free-text prompts frequently produce omissions or incorrect sequencing that violate required invariants and that prompt design and verifier choice strongly influence measured semantic-correctness [1]. Systems that integrate deterministic verifier feedback or policy-guided reranking report improved practical correctness for infrastructure-as-code and configuration-repair tasks, but effect sizes vary with verifier expressiveness and repair budget [2][3]. Formal network-verification tools (NetKAT/KATch family and related engines) provide deterministic oracles for reachability and policy checks and are commonly proposed as audit/gating layers; their protocol and scale limitations, however, affect verifier coverage and mapping effort [5]. Security analyses of agentic LLM pipelines demonstrate claim-to-action vulnerabilities (prompt-injection and tool-orchestration exploits), motivating conservative verifier gating and auditable verdicts in NetOps workflows [4]. Our trial differs from many prior evaluations in explicitly preregistering a paired estimand and enforcing shared_initial_candidate semantics so the guarded−baseline contrast isolates the marginal effect of applying at most one repair to the identical first-pass candidate.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. The study was preregistered (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) with a frozen analysis plan before any model outputs. The preregistered conceptual design described three conditions (A: baseline free-text prompt, B: constrained-template prompt, C: constrained + verifier-feedback guarded pipeline) and two confirmatory hypotheses (H1: constrained vs baseline; H2: guarded vs constrained). Execution mapping to archived run. The adapter-enforced execution semantics used in the archived run differed in operationalization from the conceptual three-condition description: the archived adapter implemented paired evaluation under shared_initial_candidate semantics with exactly one initial generation per intent that was reused across the paired baseline and guarded conditions; a guarded repair call (≤1) was permitted only if the deterministic verifier failed that initial candidate. Consequently, the archived confirmatory estimand and primary test compare guarded (C) versus baseline (A) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The preregistered constrained-only condition (B) was not executed as an independent first-pass condition in this run; therefore no confirmatory B-vs-A or C-vs-B contrasts are reported in the archived confirmatory artifacts. This mapping from preregistered labels to the executed contrast is explicit and unambiguous in the archived execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation artifact. Model and sampling. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution metadata: declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); no numeric temperature or fixed random-seed was enforced, so independent sampling nondeterminism across API sessions is possible and was anticipated in the preregistration. Execution semantics and adapter enforcement. The adapter produced exactly one shared initial generation per intent (shared_initial_generation = 150) and permitted at most one guarded repair call when the verifier failed that initial candidate (repair invocations observed = 1). Provider accounting recorded model_calls_used = 151 and completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151. These stage-level counts are artifacted in the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation. Tasks, verifier, and scoring. Confirmatory tasks (N=150) were deterministically generated by the preregistered generator and stratified across four intent families (reachability/isolation, ACL-like access, VLAN/MTU sequence changes, uplink switchover patterns). Topologies were constrained to verifier-capable small networks (4–32 nodes). Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 applied a full_intent_constraint_validation rule to produce binary pass/fail verdicts plus normalized final-configuration strings and per-episode diagnostics. Primary outcome and analysis. The primary endpoint was verifier pass (binary). The primary analysis used an exact two-sided McNemar test on paired outcomes (n_11, n_10, n_01, n_00) and computed a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistration specified complete-pair primary handling (exclude incomplete pairs) and a power target to detect a +15 percentage-point absolute improvement with N=150 under conservative discordant-pair assumptions; the run followed the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor without post-lock analytic changes.
sections.results: Execution and provider audit. The archived run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 and complete_pair_count = 150. Provider accounting: model_calls_used = 151; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0; cache_miss_count = 151. Stage counts recorded by the adapter: shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair = 1; contamination_summary.csv contains zero flags. Primary numerical outcomes. The paired contingency (guarded × baseline) was: n_11 = 149 (both-pass), n_10 = 1 (guarded-only-pass), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-pass), n_00 = 0 (both-fail). Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Estimated paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). These figures are taken verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv). Repair diagnostics and revision counts. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150), converting a single initially invalid candidate to a valid configuration under the deterministic verifier. Median revision iterations for guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). Representative validator traces (validation_before and validation_after), normalized_configuration strings, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_codes are archived for every episode; example traces for tasks 000001–000006 illustrate validator behavior across declared difficulty levels. Sensitivity and missingness. The preregistered sensitivity analysis that treats missing guarded outputs as failures was not triggered because failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0 and unscorable episodes = 0. No exclusions or parse failures occurred.
sections.discussion: Ceiling effect and inferential consequence. The preregistered power calculation assumed a substantially lower baseline success rate; the observed baseline_success_rate = 0.9933 left almost no headroom for the guarded pipeline to demonstrate the preregistered detectable effect (+15 pp). With n_11 = 149 and only a single discordant pair, the paired analysis contains very little discordant information, producing an exact McNemar p = 1.0 and a CI that includes zero. This outcome invalidated the preregistered detectable-effect assumptions and illustrates why short baseline-calibration pilots (for example, 20–40 tasks sampled from the planned generator and prompt style) should precede confirmatory sampling to estimate baseline competence and choose N or task difficulty appropriately. Sampling semantics, estimand interpretation, and operational trade-offs. We enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics so that baseline and guarded contrasts measure the marginal value of repairing the identical first-pass sampled candidate. Alternative semantics—independent per-condition sampling or multi-draw ensembles—estimate different deployment questions (expected pass rate under independent draws or benefits of re-sampling) and typically require more model calls and different power planning. Practitioners should select generation semantics that match deployment constraints (single-shot action vs resample-and-choose) and include model-call cost in power calculations. Operational affordances beyond pass/fail. Deterministic verifier outputs include normalized configurations and violation codes that increase operational observability and accelerate human triage even when a binary pass/fail contrast is small; archived validator traces demonstrate concrete diagnostic categories (missing step, order violation) that can feed automated repair policies or human review workflows. Threats to validity. Internal validity: adapter-enforced budgets and mapping unit-tests mitigated cross-condition leakage and parse/transformation errors; all unit-tests passed and contamination checks recorded zero flags. Construct validity: deterministic verifier pass/fail is a proxy for semantic correctness and depends on mapping code and verifier coverage; any uncovered verifier-coverage gap would bias the measured semantic-correctness. External validity: experiments used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic tasks on small topologies (4–32 nodes); results do not generalize to other models or production-scale heterogeneous networks. Security: this confirmatory trial did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection; separate adversary-driven evaluations are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities. Practical recommendations. From these artifact-grounded outcomes we recommend (1) a baseline-calibration pilot to estimate baseline_success_rate and discordant proportions before confirmatory sampling, (2) explicit preregistration of generation semantics and repair budgets, (3) multi-arm designs that vary repair budgets and sampling semantics to estimate cost–benefit frontiers, and (4) inclusion of provider-call accounting in power and cost planning.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired trial comparing baseline free-text prompting versus constrained-template prompting plus a single verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a deterministic synthetic corpus with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline increased verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically tiny and statistically non-significant improvement (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00,0.02]). The principal scientific lesson is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials should include baseline calibration to avoid ceiling effects and preserve inferential power. Technically, our artifacts bound the marginal benefit of a one-repair guarded pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics; evaluating independent-sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, multiple models, and production-scale topologies remains important future work.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness was far higher than the pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
